百.meaning: A chef separates egg <part>white</part> from yolk, <part>one</part> egg at a time, for the world's biggest meringue. Her arm aches and the bowl overflows. She drops the last shell on the pile and counts: she's cracked a <kanji>hundred</kanji>.
百.on: '<sound>Hee</sound>… <sound>yuck</sound>!' she giggles, wiping sticky egg off her nose.
百.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>le on a <sound>mo</sound>tor scooter delivers another hundred eggs.

貨.meaning: At the docks, crates of <part>shellfish</part> are loaded onto a ship. Halfway across the sea, they <part>change</part> into crates of pearls and coins. Whatever is inside, the captain doesn't care: to him, it's all just <kanji>freight</kanji>.
貨.on: He stamps every crate with a big orange <sound>ca</sound>rp, his ship's badge.
貨.kun: A deckhand opens one and finds a <sound>ta</sound>co, a <sound>ca</sound>rp and a crown, and cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!': treasure!

死.meaning: A skeleton chef, all <part>bones</part>, stirs a pot of soup with a long <part>spoon</part> and lifts it to taste. No tongue, no taste. 'Needs salt,' he guesses, and shrugs. That's the trouble with <kanji>death</kanji>.
死.on: He serves the soup on a knight's <sound>shie</sound>ld, since all his plates broke long ago.
死.kun: His only customer is the ghost of a <sound>shee</sound>p, who has been dead for years.

解.meaning: A <part>cow</part> wanders through a knitting shop and comes out wrapped in yarn from nose to <part>antler</part>. The owner slips a <part>sword</part> under one loop and tugs, and the knot starts to come loose, strand by strand. Slowly, she manages to <kanji>unravel</kanji> it.
解.on: Inside the tangle she finds a lost <sound>ki</sound>te, and lets it fly.
解.kun: The last strand comes off a <sound>to</sound>tem pole the cow had dragged in with it.

過.meaning: A <part>cuckoo clock</part> should call noon twelve times. This one calls a hundred, then a thousand, until it shakes itself off the wall and bounces down a <part>ramp</part>, still shouting. It always has to <kanji>overdo</kanji> it.
過.on: At the bottom it splashes into a pond, where a <sound>ca</sound>rp sits on it until it stops.
過.kun: On its way down, it rolls right past a <sound>su</sound>shi stall without stopping.
